purpose.primary: Define the privacy-first boundaries of the 5Guides learning experience.
purpose.design_goal: Support learning without building unnecessary identity, behavioral tracking, profiling, or feedback requirements around the learner.

core_principle: Learning does not grant us permission to observe the learner.
design_preference: Know less about the learner when knowing more is unnecessary.

learning_without_surveillance.principle: The learner should not have to exchange unnecessary personal information for access to the normal learning path.

domain_separation.principle: Learning, assessment, identity, analytics, feedback, and recognition should remain separate wherever practical.
domain_separation.rule: A learner who declines optional feedback has completed the same learning milestone as a learner who provides it.

identity.future_feature_boundary: If a future optional feature requires an account, that requirement should be explained separately rather than silently becoming a requirement for the learning material.

local_first.principle: Do not send information somewhere merely because it can be sent.
local_first.warning: These are design preferences, not claims about an implemented storage architecture.

private_reflection.principle: A reflection prompt does not automatically mean that the learner's response should be transmitted or stored.
learner_options: explore with an optional AI assistant

ai_boundary.principle: Choosing to use an external AI assistant changes the information boundary.
ai_boundary.learner_prompt: What am I choosing to share?
ai_boundary.service_policy_boundary: External AI services may operate under their own data practices, account requirements, retention policies, and terms.

awareness_checks.purpose: Help the learner notice what remained after first exposure and what may deserve another look.
awareness_checks.principle: An educational check does not automatically justify building a permanent behavioral record.

mastery.purpose: Determine whether the learner can use the defined skill on a fresh problem.
mastery.principle: The educational result is demonstration of the skill; that does not automatically require knowing who the learner is outside the learning interaction.

badges.rule: Receiving a badge should not automatically require a real name, email address, public account, location, school, employer, or Student Footprint.

student_footprint.purpose: Allow a learner to voluntarily leave a small feedback trace after a learning milestone.

ask_do_not_infer.principle: Volunteered information is not equivalent to silently inferred information.

country_example.preferred: Ask the learner which broad country they wish to associate with the Footprint.

country_language.reason: The intended field is a voluntarily selected broad learning location, not nationality, birthplace, ancestry, citizenship, or family background.

free_text.risk: A learner may accidentally submit identifying or sensitive information.
free_text.learner_notice: Please do not include personal or identifying information in your reflection.

analytics_boundary.principle: Curiosity about learners does not automatically justify observing them.
student_footprint_is_not_intended_to_ans: Which exercise caused them to leave?

shadow_profile.risk: Individually minor details may become identifying or behavioral when joined.
shadow_profile.principle: Privacy must be evaluated across combined records, not only one field at a time.

questions_before_collection: Could the feature work without it?
Would the learner reasonably expect us to have it?
data_minimization.rule: Do not collect tomorrow's data today.

technical_server_data.do_not_promise: No server ever receives any technical information.
technical_server_data.reason: Actual request handling depends on the eventual architecture, hosting environment, logging configuration, security controls, and services involved.
technical_server_data.design_commitment: Do not intentionally build unnecessary identity, behavioral tracking, or profiling into the learning experience.
technical_server_data.future_documentation_required: Document actual technical behavior when the implementation exists.

questions_if_implemented: Can the same purpose be achieved with less information?
logging.principle: Operational necessity should not become an excuse for unlimited collection.

retention.principle: Keeping data indefinitely requires a reason.
if_data_is_collected_ask: How long is it actually needed?

deletion_and_correction.principle: Voluntary participation should not become irreversible merely because someone submitted once.

if_implemented: avoid detailed filters that expose individuals
use additional caution with small groups

small_groups.risk: Even broad information may become identifying when very few people match it.
small_groups.default: Prefer less public precision when additional detail is unnecessary.

consent_design.principle: A meaningful choice requires a comfortable no.
avoid: making the privacy-preserving option unnecessarily difficult

privacy_theater.principle: Privacy language and observable implementation should describe the same reality.
if_mismatch_detected: do not hide the mismatch behind friendlier wording

privacy_boundaries.principle: Information crossing one system boundary may have different consequences from information remaining inside another.

awareness.question: What information actually enters the system?

alignment.question: Does each collected element correspond to a real purpose?
alignment.rule: If a field has no clear purpose, question why it exists.

coherence.question: Do implementation and privacy promises agree?
coherence.rule: Do not claim that learners are untracked while maintaining unnecessary behavioral histories.

clarity.question: Can an ordinary learner understand what happens to their information?
clarity.rule: Prefer plain language describing actual behavior.

continuity.question: If the system changes, does the privacy model still hold?
continuity.rule: Reinspect privacy whenever new features alter information flows.

core_separation.rule: The voluntary participation path must not secretly become a requirement of the student learning path.

success_condition.description: Support the learning experience without building unnecessary machinery for watching the learner.
success_condition.acceptable_outcome: For information the system deliberately chose not to collect, the honest answer may be: we do not know.
success_condition.principle: Not knowing unnecessary information is a privacy outcome, not automatically an analytics failure.

must: Treat learning, mastery, badges, and optional feedback as separate domains.
Preserve learner uncertainty and privacy choices.
Avoid requesting identifying information when the learning task does not require it.
Distinguish learner-provided information from inferred information.
State when implementation details are not defined.
Reinspect privacy boundaries when discussing new features.
must_not: claim that no technical data reaches a server without implementation evidence
turn assessment responses into research data by default
build unsupported demographic conclusions from Footprints
silently broaden the purpose of collected information
